author: MiYu
scope: Stable equal-priority navigation shared by generated client and authoritative Node server.
rootCause: Math.hypot rounding changes nearly equal A* heap priorities across QuickJS and V8, selecting different routes.
rule: Quantize only heap priorities with Math.round(score * 1e9); retain true path costs, coordinates and collision rules. Integer heap ordering remains transitive.
compatibility: Some TD and MOBA tied paths and subsequent battle outcomes change. Existing saves still load. This is a path-selection rule change, not a claim of exact legacy trajectories.

regression.scope: Captured TD divergence input with alternate QuickJS/V8 hypot rounding, full state comparison every frame, exact integer/structure checks and unchanged 1e-8 float bound; includes legacy-state loading and mid-match save restore.

negativeControl.description: Removing priority quantization fails the captured frame-324 route assertion.

serverRuntime.scope: Actual server simulation module versus generated rules in native QuickJS and V8 for each matrix workload. Complete final-state comparison, exact integer/structure checks and unchanged 1e-8 float bound. This is not a two-machine network test or engine-bridge acceptance.

limitations: Native CPU benchmark is not Editor FPS or full engine bridge acceptance.
Integer A* priorities intentionally change some previously tied TD and MOBA routes; workload timings are not purely geometry optimization comparisons.
Cross-runtime float comparisons retain the existing 1e-8 bound; integers and structures compare exactly.
110-unit QuickJS simulation remains about 516 ms per step; observed cold maximum 1039.1123 ms can exceed the production one-second deadline.
Actual server module comparisons and local TCP tests do not establish two-machine native-client acceptance.
